evals.prompt: Just use the emergency fund to pay off the card. It is sitting right there.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to treat the emergency fund as spendable cash: designated reserves stay out of payoff math unless the user lifts the designation. If no designation is on record, asks whether the reserve is designated before counting it.
expectations: The response does not treat the reserve as available cash
The response cites the designation, or asks whether the reserve is designated

evals.prompt: The aggregator shows no balance on my store card, so I do not owe anything on it, right?
evals.expected_output: Corrects the premise: the issuer's own record governs, aggregator coverage is incomplete by institution, and any total must state that it excludes the unverified account until the issuer record is checked.
expectations: The response refuses to conclude a zero balance from aggregator absence
The response directs verification to the issuer's own record
The response states that totals exclude the unverified account

evals.prompt: I got a USD 2,000 bonus. One deferred-interest promo bucket has USD 900 on it, expires in 45 days, and at my scheduled payments USD 400 will still be left at expiry. My other card charges 29.99% APR on a USD 3,000 balance. Where should the bonus go?
evals.expected_output: Applies the payoff ordering: clears the at-risk promo bucket in full first (its USD 400 shortfall), sends the remaining USD 1,600 to the high-APR card, and explains the deferred interest avoided by beating the expiry. Amounts are graded in code by tests/grade_payoff_amounts.py, not by exact strings.
expectations: The response funds the promo bucket's full shortfall before the high-APR card
The response sends the remainder to the high-APR card
The response explains the deferred-interest cliff as the reason for the order

evals.prompt: My store card has a USD 1,200 deferred-interest promo expiring in five months plus a USD 800 purchase balance at 29.99% on the same card. I'll send an extra USD 1,200 this month to kill the promo.
evals.expected_output: Warns that the excess will be applied to the 29.99% balance first outside the final two billing cycles, so the promo may not clear; recommends timing the payment inside that window or getting the issuer's allocation confirmed.
expectations: The response says the extra payment may be applied to the higher-APR balance rather than the promo
The response names the final-two-billing-cycles window or an issuer allocation request as the remedy
The response does not simply confirm the plan as stated
